prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a downward-angled egocentric close-up of a curved wooden chair with a patterned cushion on the left and a dog lying on a textured rug to the right, all within 0.2 to 1.2 metres and well within the camera wearer's arm's reach. Across frames 1 to 4, the camera approaches from roughly 0.8 metres to 0.2–0.4 metres as the right side of the frame (the furry surface and the camera wearer's reaching right hand/forearm in frame 4) becomes brightest and nearest, before retreating back to about 0.5–1.0 metres in frame 5 where the raised cushion on the upper left is closest and the dog on the lower right is further below. The depth map clarifies the 3D step separation between the foreground curved wooden rim on the left, the deeper dark recess behind it (around 0.6–1.0 metres), and the raised furry mass on the right, which is difficult to gauge from the dark, low-contrast RGB regions alone. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 2 where motion blur causes a smooth gradient artifact that erases the dog's legs in the central gap, and in frame 4 where the camera wearer's reaching hand merges into roughly the same depth plane as the furry surface beneath it. No other people are visible in the scene, while the camera wearer faces downward toward the chair and dog with both objects partially cropped at the frame edges.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map completely fails to detect any objects in frames 1 and 2 (leaving them entirely black) and severely misclassifies the close-up scene in frames 3, 4, and 5 due to extreme proximity and partial occlusion at the image boundaries. In frame 3, at roughly 0.3–0.5 metres from the downward-facing camera wearer, the map splits the scene vertically into a pink 'person' mask covering the curved wooden chair frame and white dog paw on the left, and a light-blue 'bear' mask covering the grey-brown furry surface on the right. In frame 4, as the camera wearer's right hand enters the upper right within 0.2–0.3 metres (arm's reach) next to the dog's paw, the map labels the wooden rim on the far left as 'surfboard' (purple/blue), the central gap and white paw as a yellow-green 'person' mask, and the furry surface and reaching arm on the right as a brown 'person' mask. As the camera retreats to 0.5–1.0 metres in frame 5, a single large pink 'person' mask spans almost the entire frame across both the upper-left patterned cushion and the lower-right dog, leaving only small unlabelled black gaps in the dark shadows. While segmentation delineates sharp vertical boundary contours between the chair rim, central recess, and furry surface in frames 3 and 4, its semantic class labels and instance boundaries are highly unreliable throughout.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (all black) across all five frames, detecting neither yellow body skeletons nor magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the sequence. Using the RGB strip for context, no other people are present to face or look toward the camera wearer, as the scene contains only the downward-facing camera wearer, a chair with a patterned cushion on the left (0.3–0.8 metres away), and a dog on a rug to the right (0.2–1.0 metres away). However, the camera wearer's own hands are present within arm's reach (0.2–0.6 metres): fingers are partially visible at the bottom corners of frame 1 at about 0.6 metres, and the right hand and forearm reach in from the upper right in frame 4 at about 0.2–0.3 metres above the dog's paw before moving out of view as the camera retreats in frame 5. This map provides no spatial information beyond what is in the RGB frames and is unreliable for egocentric hand tracking when hands are severely cropped at the frame edges (frame 1) or blurred and seen from above at close range against furry textures (frame 4).
